subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should OpenClaw stop propagating host workspace overrides into third-party managed npm plugin roots, add targeted Express 4 validation, or keep the current behavior and require plugin-local overrides?
rationale: The issue is valid, but the repair changes the dependency-ownership boundary between OpenClaw's reviewed override policy and third-party plugin package graphs; automation should not choose that policy by itself.

options.title: Scope managed overrides
options.body: Prefer a narrow managed-root policy that keeps OpenClaw's own security overrides where needed while avoiding corruption of third-party plugin dependency graphs, with tests and docs.

options.title: Validator-only diagnostic
options.body: Add detection for known incompatible Express 4/path-to-regexp graphs and fail with an actionable message while leaving dependency resolution ownership unchanged.

options.title: Require plugin-local fixes
options.body: Keep current OpenClaw behavior and document that affected plugin packages must pin or upgrade their own Express/path-to-regexp dependency tree.

recommendation.title: Scope managed overrides
recommendation.body: Prefer a narrow managed-root policy that keeps OpenClaw's own security overrides where needed while avoiding corruption of third-party plugin dependency graphs, with tests and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The current source and blame evidence tie vincentkoc to the managed npm override path and workspace override surface most directly.
